subject: SaaSify - tiered commit & premium-model allocation (follow-up)
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@saasify.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@saasify.ai>
Date: 2026-10-31 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing ask: commit tiers + model mix

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo today — the latency numbers look promising. Our finance team is running a model for annual spend and asked me to get a firm proposal for: (1) a 12-month commit with monthly reconciliation, and (2) how committed units would be allocated if we use a mix of standard chat + a small % of premium models and embeddings-heavy workloads.

A couple of clarifying Qs up front:
- Does the premium-model surcharge apply to embedding calls or only to generation/chat?
- How do unused committed tokens behave — credit rollover, conversion to prepaid credits, or forfeiture?
- Can we get an example P&L at three commit levels (100M, 500M, 2B tokens) showing blended per-token effective price if premium models account for 20% of generation and embeddings are 30% of calls?

Can you send a short proposal and ballpark effective rates so we can run it through procurement? Tom and I are looping procurement next week.

Best,
Lydia

--
Lydia Park
Head of ML Platforms, SaaSify
lydia.park@saasify.ai
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@saasify.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02 10:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing ask: commit tiers + model mix

Lydia —

Appreciate the details and the thoughtful questions. Attached is a short proposal (saasify_proposal_v1.pdf) and a decision table; summary below to help procurement. I kept the structure simple so legal/finance can map it to a PO.

High level proposal (12-month commit, monthly billing against committed tokens):
- Commit tiers considered: 100M, 500M, 2B tokens/month (we can also do annualized tokens).
- Base per-token rates (hosted API, standard chat model): $0.0008 / token.
- Premium model surcharge: +150% on base (i.e., premium chat = $0.0020 / token).
- Embedding calls: priced per-embedding unit; standard embedding = $0.0025 / embedding call. Premium embedding model = +100% surcharge (i.e., $0.0050).

Blended example (500M commit, monthly):
- Assumptions: 20% generation on premium models, 30% of total calls are embeddings (standard), remaining generation on standard chat.
- Effective blended per-token (generation+embeddings apportioned to token-equivalent): ~$0.00105 / token (this includes embedding units normalized at our typical tokens-per-embed factor — see attached table).

Unused commit handling options (pick one):
A) 12-month term, monthly true-up: unused tokens expire at month-end (standard).
B) Convert unused tokens to one-time credits at 80% of face value, usable across Redwood hosted products for 12 months.
C) Rollover up to 10% of monthly unused tokens to next month; any beyond expire.

Operational notes:
- We can lock in premium-model allocation floors (e.g., up to 25% premium without extra commit) or charge on usage above that floor.
- Burst capacity above commit is available at on-demand rates (no surcharge) or via pre-purchased burst bundles (recommended for predictable peaks).

Next steps 
1) Tell us which unused-commit policy you prefer (A/B/C).
2) Confirm whether premium surcharge should apply to embeddings for your use case — we can carve it out or apply it uniformly.
3) If acceptable, we’ll convert the proposal to a draft SOW and route to legal.

I copied Marissa and Aditya (pricing/legal) for visibility.

Thanks,
Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Pricing ask: commit tiers + model mix

Looping in a few practical guardrails from our side:
- For enterprise deals we typically recommend Option B for unused-commit (convert at 80% credit) for strategic customers; it simplifies procurement and reduces sticker shock.
- Suggest a hybrid surcharge for embeddings: standard embedding rate for vector-only operations (search/indexing), premium surcharge only when premium embedding model demonstrably improves quality (measured via evals). We can include a 30-day evaluation window where premium embedding calls are billed at standard rate pending quality signoff.
- For the blended pricing table, we should present two scenarios: (i) premium-surcharge-applies-to-embeddings, (ii) premium-surcharge-exempt-for-embeddings-during-PO-eval. This helps procurement see upside.

Operational asks for Lydia/Tom to confirm:
1) Preferred unused-commit policy (we recommend B).
2) Target % of traffic you expect to hit premium chat in month 1 vs month 6 (helps us size dedicated capacity).
3) Whether you need SLA-backed latency targets (we can include a Dedicated capacity add-on if required).

I’ll work with Aditya to convert the summary into PO-friendly language and a short schedule of rates that legal can attach. Rafael — once Lydia confirms the first two items we can push a draft SOW.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Pricing ask: commit tiers + model mix

Thanks team — quick follow after procurement reviewed the attachment. They sent a redline (attached: SaaSify_PO_redline_20261105.pdf) and asked two concrete clarifications before we can issue a PO: 
1) Confirm that embeddings used for semantic search (indexing + similarity) will be billed at the standard embedding rate during a 30-day POC even if they use a premium embedding model; any premium uplift to apply only after mutual signoff.
2) Request explicit callout in the SOW that unused tokens converted to credits under option B will be usable across both hosted API and Dedicated offerings (procurement wants portability).

Can Redwood confirm these two items in writing so we can attach to the PO and route to legal? Also, procurement wants a single-line effective blended rate for the 500M tier (month 1) under both embedding-charge scenarios — can you provide that as a single-dollar-per-token figure?

We’re aiming to get a PO out this week if we can lock the two bullets above.

Thanks,
Tom
